subject: Request: custom availability amendment for order form
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acadiahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Acadia Procurement <procurement@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom availability amendment for order form

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a narrow request so we can close the order form and attach it to the MSA. Two asks from legal/ops:

1) Availability SLO: they require a defined monthly availability percentage and a clear credit calculation.
2) Latency commitment: they want a p95 inference latency target for our hosted inference path (their workflows are latency-sensitive).

We understand Redwood's standard SLA, but Acadia needs the following variations for this engagement:

- Monthly Availability (Monthly Uptime Percentage): 99.95% for the production model endpoint tied to the order form.
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 500 ms for requests with sequence lengths <= 1024 tokens, measured at the API gateway for the production route.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance >= 48 hours' notice, force majeure, and customer-induced network issues.
- Remedies: service credits calculated as a percentage of monthly fees tied to the impacted route, escalated to a 50% credit if availability < 99.0% for the billing month.

I've attached a draft order form (Acadia_Draft_OrderForm_20261005.pdf) and a redline of the MSA showing where they want the order-form referenced. Can your team review and propose specific addendum language we can attach to the SOW/order form? Procurement is targeting signature by the end of next week if we can agree quickly.

Thanks — I copied procurement and legal will loop if they have additional tweaks.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Cloud Integrations
Acadia Health
[Attachment: Acadia_Draft_OrderForm_20261005.pdf]
[Attachment: redlined_msa_ACD-3092.docx]

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom availability amendment for order form

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. We're happy to work through a focused SLA addendum that can be appended to the order form. Next steps from our side:

1) Marissa (legal) will propose precise addendum wording that maps to your bullets.
2) Karthik (solutions) will validate the p95 / 500 ms latency target against the expected traffic profile and confirm any carve-outs for large-batch/streaming requests.
3) I'll coordinate a single redline you can circulate to your legal/procurement.

Quick note on latency: we can commit to a p95 <= 500 ms for inference routed through our hosted API on the production route under steady-state single-request traffic; we'll call out exclusions for bulk batch jobs and for requests that exceed the token-length expectation. We'll also propose an objective measurement point (api.redwood.com -> production route) and an agreed sampling window for monthly calculations.

Can you confirm whether the order form's fees are monthly recurring charges tied to the production route (so credits are applied against that line item)? If so we'll include the prorated credit calculation in the addendum.

I'll queue this for Marissa and Karthik; expect a redline back by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: custom availability amendment for order form (SLA addendum language)

Elena / Connor —

Attached is a draft SLA addendum we can attach to the order form. High-level summary below and then the exact redline language is in the attachment (sla_addendum_template.docx). If this maps to Acadia's needs you can attach it to the order form and we can produce a single redline for the MSA references.

Summary of proposed commitments:
- Monthly Availability (Monthly Uptime Percentage): 99.95% measured per calendar month for the production endpoint(s) specified in the Order Form.
- Latency Commitment: p95 inference latency <= 500 ms for requests <= 1024 tokens, measured at Redwood's public API gateway for the production route, using production traffic sampling.
- Measurement and Reporting: Redwood will provide a monthly SLA report (UTC) with uptime percentage, p95 latency, and sample sizes. Reports will be delivered via shared Drive link and are auditable by Acadia upon 30 days' notice.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (>=48 hours' prior notice), customer-originated network issues, force majeure, and any degradation caused by customer payloads that deviate from the agreed token length or rate profile.
- Remedy / Credits: For availability below 99.95% but >= 99.0% in a billed month, Acadia shall be eligible to receive a credit equal to 10% of the monthly fee attributed to the impacted route. For availability < 99.0% in a billed month, the credit shall be 50% of the monthly fee for the impacted route. Credits are exclusive and limited to the stated remedies.
- Latency breaches will trigger a one-time credit equal to 5% of the monthly fee for the impacted route for the first occurrence in a rolling 12-month period; recurring latency breaches will be escalated to remediation planning and may trigger additional credits at Redwood's discretion.

We included precise calculation formulas in the addendum (sample math for pro rata credits) and a short operational definition of "availability" for the production route (time-in-state measured at the API ingress). We also added a short-runbook requirement: Redwood will initiate a joint incident review if either availability < 99.0% in a month or latency p95 > 750 ms for two consecutive weeks.

Please review the attached language; if you'd like I can produce a version that uses your Order Form fee line items for the credit math so procurement has an executable redline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: custom availability amendment for order form (SLA addendum language)

Hi Marissa / Connor —

Thank you — the language looks good and aligns with what legal wanted. A couple quick points before we finalize:

1) For the latency remedy, can we make the first credit for p95 breaches cumulative with availability credits if both are breached in the same billing month? Legal prefers clear stacking rules. If Redwood prefers exclusivity, please state that explicitly.
2) Procurement would like the SLA report to be delivered to procurement@acadiahealth.com and to include the raw sample size numbers used to compute p95.

If you confirm point (1) as exclusive (credits do not stack) then procurement will accept and we can route to signature. If your team agrees to allow stacking (availability + latency credits), procurement has requested an upper limit cap of 60% total credit for a single billing month.

Procurement is ready to sign once we have the final redline. Can you send a DocuSign link for the amended Order Form + SLA addendum when you're ready?

Best,
—Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Cloud Integrations
Acadia Health
